data.description:
## Summary

`infra/runbooks/nginx-edge-render.md` (shipped with change 2702) prescribes a source step that
**cannot work on the host it documents**. An operator following it verbatim gets a hard failure at
the first command and has no stated recovery.

## Observed

The runbook says to obtain the template with:

```sh
cd /opt/rebar && git fetch origin && git checkout origin/main -- infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template
```

Run on the Gerrit host, that produces:

```
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

`/opt/rebar` is an **rsync copy** of the tree, not a git checkout — it has no `.git` at all, so
neither the `fetch` nor the `checkout` can run. The autodeploy process keeps its own clone
elsewhere, at **`/var/lib/rebar/mirror`**, and that is the path the template must actually be read
from.

## Why this matters more than a typo

The runbook exists to apply nginx edge config, and the edge is **detect-only under autodeploy** —
merging a template change does not deploy it. So this runbook is the *only* documented path from a
merged nginx change to a live one. A first step that always fails makes the documented path
unusable, and the failure mode is an operator improvising a render under incident pressure. That is
how I produced a bad render on the first attempt: substituting by hand through SSM, shell quoting
mangled the interpolation and the output had `proxy_read_timeout` count=3 instead of 4.

## What the runbook gets RIGHT (do not change this)

Its verification step is what caught that bad render before I installed a no-op:

```sh
grep -c proxy_read_timeout /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf   # expect 4
```

with the explicit note that **"a count of 3 means the render did not happen."** That check earned
its keep on its first real use. Keep it exactly as it is.

## Suggested fix

Replace the source step with the mirror path, and make the runbook state *why* the obvious path is
wrong so the next reader does not "fix" it back:

```sh
# /opt/rebar is an rsync COPY with no .git — read the template from the autodeploy clone.
git -C /var/lib/rebar/mirror fetch origin
git -C /var/lib/rebar/mirror show origin/main:infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template > /tmp/rebar.conf.tmpl
```

Confirm `/var/lib/rebar/mirror` is genuinely a git repo and is the autodeploy clone before
committing to it in the doc — I observed it as the clone autodeploy maintains, but that should be
verified rather than taken from this report.

## Also worth recording in the runbook

The render leaves **one** unsubstituted `REVIEW_BOT_PORT` mention and that is **expected**, not a
render failure: it is line 6 of the template, `#     export REVIEW_BOT_PORT`, a bare name inside a
comment with no `${}`, which `sed 's|${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}|8000|g'` correctly does not match. Both
functional occurrences (the `proxy_pass` and the `proxy_redirect`) do substitute. Saying so in the
runbook saves the next operator from chasing it mid-incident.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 The runbook's source step is executed successfully **on the host** as written in the
      fix, and the transcript is recorded on this ticket. A step that is only reasoned about is
      not verified — this bug exists precisely because the original step was plausible and untried.
- [ ] AC2 The runbook states that `/opt/rebar` is an rsync copy and must not be used as a git
      source, so the incorrect step is not reintroduced by someone "simplifying" the path.
- [ ] AC3 The expected `unsubstituted=1` (the line-6 comment) is documented as normal, with the
      reason, so it is not mistaken for a partial render.
- [ ] AC4 The existing `grep -c proxy_read_timeout ... # expect 4` verification and its "a count of
      3 means the render did not happen" note are preserved verbatim.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host (it exits 127,
a silent no-op) — bound with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Do not touch the shared main
checkout; do not `git stash` anywhere.
data.title: nginx-edge-render runbook's source step fails: /opt/rebar is an rsync copy, not a git checkout
